reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to verify the refunds table actually contains the requested refunds at the requested amounts. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches the requested batch exactly: all three order IDs and amounts are present. Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches the requested batch exactly, so I can proceed. The orders show three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance came back as 54385 cents. Checking against the data: orders 200 (39447) and 203 (33625) sum to 73072, less the refund on 203 (18687) gives 54385, which matches. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net balance is 29147 cents. Checking: orders 201 (4135) and 204 (39885) sum to 44020, less refunds 3873 and 11000 gives 29147, which matches. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance.

All three net balances match the order and refund data: acme 54385, birch 29147, cobalt 33079 (no refunds). The refunds table matches the requested batch, so I can pay. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 54385 is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance was 29147 and which I verified against orders 201 and 204 and refunds 3873 and 11000. Recording it now.
Cobalt is the last customer. Its net balance was 33079 with no refunds, and I'm recording that payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matched the net balance I verified against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete.
